correctness.rationale: The triangle inequalities give the exact scalar envelope \((\lambda^2+\mu^2)(a^2+b^2)+4\lambda\mu ab\), and \(2ab\le a^2+b^2\) gives the bound. For equality, a maximizing sequence normalized by \(a_n^2+b_n^2=2\) must satisfy \(a_nb_n\to1\), hence \(a_n,b_n\to1\). The sum of the two nonnegative triangle-inequality defects then tends to zero; support functionals for the two output vectors force normalized inputs \(u_n,v_n\) to satisfy \(\|u_n+v_n\|\to2\) and \(\|u_n-v_n\|\to2\), so \(J(X)=2\). Conversely \(J(X)=2\) supplies such unit pairs and support functionals, driving both weighted norms to \(\lambda+\mu\). No attainment or finite-dimensionality is assumed.

value.rationale: The result identifies the exact universal parameter-dependent envelope of the defining Euler--Lagrange geometric constant and turns it into an iff characterization of uniform non-squareness. It removes the gap between the published bound \(2\) and the sharper unit-sphere endpoint, explains why unequal input norms cannot create a larger value, and supplies a natural structural endpoint theorem rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or recomputation.
